messages:
emma: Heads up — hit a subtle redaction/correlation mismatch in the Go and Node sampleapps when a retry path flips log level. Traces have req_id but some logs show `<redacted>`.

riley: Can you paste the minimal steps and a tiny log snippet?

emma: Steps: start sampleapps with REDACT=1 LOG_LEVEL=info OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318; call /auth which simulates a 401 then 200 (retry). Logs:```
INFO auth: start user=zoe req_id=req-42
DEBUG http: refresh attempt=1
INFO auth: done user=zoe req_id=<redacted>
```
Trace span shows attribute req_id=req-42 for entire trace. Only final INFO got redacted.

chris: My bet: redaction runs as a formatting hook that inspects rendered message text before span attrs are attached, so when the retry path emits the final log the structured field isn't visible to the redactor.

riley: Quick mitigation: create the span with req_id as an attribute at the top of the handler and stash req_id in the request context. That way formatting/redaction can prefer structured fields. Example (Go):
```
spanCtx := tracer.Start(ctx, "request", trace.WithAttributes(attribute.String("req_id", reqID)))
ctx = spanCtx
// pass ctx down so loggers can read req_id from context
```
This removed the race for me locally.

emma: Node pattern is similar — attach req_id to req.context and start span immediately. Also reorder middleware so the redaction/formatter runs after span is initialized or make redactor consult span attributes.

chris: Long term: change library redaction to check span attributes first (structured), then fallback to string-redaction. Regexing formatted text is fragile with async exporters and batching.

riley: I'll add a couple tiny PRs: (1) update sampleapps to attach req_id early and add comments in quickstart; (2) add a smoke test that toggles a retry to reproduce; (3) open a follow-up to make the redact middleware span-aware.

ops-bot: Created TASK-7782: "sampleapps: deterministic req_id propagation and redaction during retry flows" -> https://redwood.internal/TASK-7782

emma: Thanks. If folks hit this in other runtimes drop short logs into the ticket so we can generalize.

chris: Also adding a short note in the DX onboarding doc explaining why ordering matters — it confuses new users.
